title: Homogeneous invertible modules on an abelian variety are algebraically trivial
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $A/k$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety], and let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_A$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For $a\in A(k)$ write $t_a:A\to A$ for translation $x\mapsto x+a$ under the group law; pullback is tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback]. If $t_a^*L\cong L$ for every $a\in A(k)$, then $L$ is algebraically equivalent to $\mathcal O_A$. Here algebraic equivalence is the equivalence relation on invertible-module isomorphism classes generated by pairs of fibres of an invertible module on $A\times_k T$, with $T$ a smooth connected $k$-variety. There is no restriction on the characteristic of $k$ or the dimension of $A$.

source.place: Chapter I §8, Proposition 8.4(b) and definition of Pic^0(A), printed pp.35–36; Remark 8.7(c), printed p.37, and Proposition 8.14 and its following family construction, printed pp.39–40. The homogeneous Pic^0 classes are realized as fibres of a connected smooth parameter family.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-abelian-variety-projective], choose an ample invertible module $M$ on $A$. The hypothesis of that theorem is precisely that $A$ is an abelian variety; it has no dimension or characteristic restriction.

source.place: I Theorem 6.2 (projectivity); I §8 Proposition 8.14 (choose an ample sheaf)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ample-translation-difference-surjectivity] to this $M$ and the given $L$. Its hypotheses are the algebraic closedness of $k$, the abelian variety $A$, ampleness of $M$, and the assumed invariance $t_b^*L\cong L$ for all $b\in A(k)$. Obtain $a\in A(k)$ and an isomorphism $L\cong t_a^*M\otimes M^{-1}$. This is the surjectivity of Milne’s $\lambda_M$ onto his homogeneously defined $\operatorname{Pic}^0(A)$, without identifying that definition with algebraic equivalence.

source.place: I Proposition 8.14, printed p.39, and Proposition 8.4(b), printed pp.35–36

proof.text: On $A\times_k A$ let $m$ be addition and $p_1$ the first projection, and set $\mathcal F=m^*M\otimes p_1^*(M^{-1})$. This is an invertible module: a local basis $e$ for $M$ gives the dual basis $e^{-1}$ for $M^{-1}$; on intersections of the inverse images of trivializing opens for the two maps, their pulled-back bases have tensor product a basis for $\mathcal F$. These opens cover the product. This verifies local rank one directly from [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For $b\in A(k)$ put $i_b(x)=(x,b)$. Since $m i_b=t_b$ and $p_1i_b=\mathrm{id}_A$, composition of tensor pullbacks gives $i_b^*\mathcal F\cong t_b^*M\otimes M^{-1}$. Pullback commutes with this tensor product by the local formula $B\otimes_R(P\otimes_RQ)\cong(B\otimes_RP)\otimes_B(B\otimes_RQ)$, $b\otimes(p\otimes q)\mapsto(b\otimes p)\otimes(1\otimes q)$. Thus $i_0^*\mathcal F\cong M\otimes M^{-1}\cong\mathcal O_A$ by evaluation and $i_a^*\mathcal F\cong L$ by step 2.

source.place: I §8 opening family m^*M tensor p^*M^{-1}, printed p.34; family construction following Proposition 8.14, printed pp.39–40

proof.text: Take the second copy of $A$ as the parameter variety $T$. It is smooth and connected by [def-sc-abelian-variety]. The single family $\mathcal F$ therefore has two fibres, at $0$ and $a$, representing $\mathcal O_A$ and $L$. By the definition of algebraic equivalence in the item these classes are related by a generating pair, so $L$ is algebraically equivalent to $\mathcal O_A$. This also covers $a=0$ and $\dim A=0$; the definition does not require distinct parameter points.

source.place: I §8, family following Proposition 8.14, printed pp.39–40; algebraic equivalence as defined in the item
